# Exemplars and benchmark lenses

Teaching examples are not endorsements of entire estimates. Best practice combines methods across collections.

| Benchmark | Observed exemplar | Lesson and qualification |
|---|---|---|
| Best individual recent total score | BLS SOII202404-1220-001,83 | Transparent activity/sector/year tables and obligation boundaries; federal budget detail remains weak. |
| Strongest Item12 composite | BLS SOII and NCS202310-1220-004,53/60 | Direct compensation, segmentation, nonresponse and phases; TSA flight training is close at52/60. |
| Compact reproducibility | SEC ADV-E202409-3235-022 | A small model can expose essential arithmetic efficiently; narrow scope limits comparison. |
| Item13 purchased services | OSHA extinguishers202405-1218-005; FCC satellite202505-3060-038 | Quantities, make-or-buy and prices/ranges; consultation age and scope need review. |
| Capital methodology, historical | EPA CEMS SRC-0161/0162 | Principal, life, discount and recurring costs; old prices and broader regulatory scope require mapping. No universal recent nonzero capital winner. |
| Item14 workload methods | TSA aircraft202406-1652-001 and airports202412-1652-001; EPA CSAPR202505-2060-004; FAA repair202404-2120-002 | Workload times hours times compensation; some pay/contract inputs remain unavailable. Highest score9 is EBSA settlement's justified incremental zero, not a nonzero cost model. |
| Strongest Item15 | FCC IPCS202503-3060-020,10/10 | Exact obligation bridge and public-notice revision; assumption quality is separate from arithmetic. |
| Highest agency-level quality | Not established | Means are descriptive; heterogeneous purposive cases cannot establish a population rank. |
| Most consistent agency | Not established | Dataset includes mean, range and dispersion; small repeated samples are not representative. |
| TSA-relevant comparators | OSHA process safety202508-1218-005,80; Coast Guard security202408-1625-012,77; CMMC202405-0704-002,75 | Complex regulatory work, security plans and phased assessments; scope differs and small score differences should not determine adoption. |
| Validation | Census AIES SRC-0099 printed page19 | Respondent studies, questionnaire reports and paradata have different scopes; medians are not means. |
| Shared PRA/RIA methodology | EBSA SRC-0102; CMMC SRC-0164 | Direct evidence of analytical reuse beyond PRA clearance; worked examples and scope still need checking. |

Full ties: leaders.md. Descriptive agency statistics: data/agency-summary.csv. Federal best practice includes transferable statistical methods; TSA-relevant practice emphasizes private-sector compliance, security, records, systems, occupations and regulatory reuse.

Descriptive repeated-component lens (n>=3 only): BLS has the highest observed mean76.67(n3); Census has the narrowest observed score dispersion1.41(n3,range71–74). These are within-sample summaries, not agency population rankings.

# Frozen observed leaders — M1-1.0.0

Reviewed: 73. Scores measure accessible documentation. One-point differences are not evidence of meaningful superiority. Ties are preserved.

| Dimension | Score | Observed ICRs |
|---|---:|---|
| total_score | 83 | 202404-1220-001 |
| reproducibility | 20 | 202409-3235-022 |
| provenance | 12 | 202404-1220-001; 202405-1652-001 |
| segmentation | 15 | 202310-0607-003; 202310-1219-001; 202310-1220-004; 202312-2050-001; 202401-2070-005; 202401-3235-005; 202404-1220-001; 202405-0704-002; 202405-1652-001; 202406-1652-001; 202410-0960-002; 202410-3150-005; 202412-1652-001; 202502-0960-015; 202502-2040-002; 202504-1652-008; 202508-1218-005; 202509-2060-003; 202511-0583-005; 202511-1545-005; 202602-2060-006; 202603-0535-001; 202603-1210-004 |
| labor | 8 | 202310-1220-004; 202405-0704-002; 202405-1218-005; 202405-1652-001; 202411-1651-004; 202411-2070-003; 202412-1205-002 |
| item13 | 10 | 202310-0607-003; 202403-0607-001; 202404-1220-001; 202602-0607-001 |
| item14 | 9 | 202501-1210-006 |

Item12 spans reproducibility, provenance, segmentation and labor; do not call a single column the Item12 winner. SEC ADV-E is concise; BLS SOII has the highest observed overall score. Census AIES supplies direct measurement triangulation. FCC IPCS supplies an exact change bridge.

Legitimate Item13 zeros are eligible for full credit. Nonzero purchased-service exemplars include OSHA extinguishers and FCC satellite. EPA monitoring gives explicit capital/O&M separation but incomplete annuity inputs. No fully validated nonzero capital leader is established.

Agency means and dispersion are descriptive (data/agency-summary.csv). Highest agency-level quality and most consistent agency are not established from these heterogeneous purposive cases.

Among components with at least three sampled controls, BLS has the highest observed mean76.67(n3,range69–83), while Census has the narrowest observed dispersion(SD1.41,n3,range71–74). The n>=3 convention is a descriptive display filter, not a representativeness or reliability threshold. Neither establishes federal agency-wide superiority or consistency.
requirements-floor:
# Governing instructions and analytical enhancements
Verified sources: SRC-0001 (current-hosted general instructions,undated) and SRC-0002 (ROCIS PRA Module User Guide,v9.0,June2026); current 5CFR1320.3 and1320.8 and OIRA-maintained Digital.gov burden guidance supplement these.

## Required PRA compliance and submission instructions
- Item12: respondents,frequency,annualhours,estimationmethod;separate forms;appropriate laborcategories. Instructions call for ranges and explanation when burdens vary widely. Consultation is desirable;do not commission a special survey solely for estimates unless directed.
- Item13: annual non-hour costs,capital/startup annualized over useful life,separate O&M/services;methods,life,discount rate andcost timing whereapplicable;explain variation. Exclude alreadycounted labor andusual/customary ornon-informationcollection compliance costs.
- Item14: annualized federal costs andmethod,including quantified hours andincremental operating expenses. A program's entire budget is not automatically a collection cost.
- Item15: explain programchanges andadjustments. ROCIS separately records changes attributable to statute,agency discretion,estimate adjustment andpotential PRA violations. June2026 guide pp49–51 defines adjustments as changes notresulting from deliberate federal action.
- 5CFR1320.8(a)(4) requires a specific objectively supported estimate. Evidentiary support is not merely optional analytical sophistication.

## Enhanced analytical practice
Reproducible formula files;atomic activities andlineage;input-level source dates/identifiers;automatic dimensional checks;complete old-to-new driver decomposition;explicit uncertainty commensurate with significance;versioned price andpolicy baselines;separate social-resource costs from fees/transfers andbudget effects;source-aware deterministic tables andprose.
These are enhancements to documentation,reusability andauditability. They must not be misrepresented as a uniform statutory requirement for a particular software format.

## Instruction defects and interpretation register
Both SRC-0001 Item12 and SRC-0002 appendix route outside-party costs to federal cost in wording that conflicts with Item13's explicit inclusion of purchased informationcollection services. Operational ROCIS cost-burden instructions andthe economic identity ofthe payer support distinguishing respondent-paid services inItem13 from government-paid contracts inItem14. Preserve this as an interpretation,not a silently altered quotation;confirm with agency PRA/OIRA guidance before hardcoding.
The June2026 appendix also gives the optional combined table sentence its own number15,shifting the change question to16. Use the semantic Items12–15 convention inthis mission;record the source numbering defect so citations do not drift.
PRA burden scope anddownstream regulatory cost scope are related butnot identical. The tool needs separate ledgers andexplicit mapping;do not treat all compliance expenditures orfees as equivalent welfare costs.

# Research-derived tool requirements — provisional v0.5.0

This is a specification for later development. No modeling application has been built. Evidence references identify a useful method or observed failure; they do not endorse the entire collection.

| ID | Behavior | Empirical basis | Acceptance condition |
|---|---|---|---|
| TR-01 | Inputs carry source, locator, date, price year, unit and transformation. | TSA HME and CBP pipeline, SRC-0054/0044 | An input ledger traces the final value through all transformations. |
| TR-02 | Generate tables and prose from one model version. | CFPB HMDA, SRC-0052 | Title, legal authority and every total agree across outputs. |
| TR-03 | Preserve exact units and precision until display. | FRA HOS, SRC-0070 | Eight minutes remains 8/60 hours, not .13. |
| TR-04 | Distinguish unique respondents, responses, assets, sites and chemicals. | EPA TRI and OSHA extinguishers, SRC-0062/0060 | Repeated activity rows do not inflate unique respondents. |
| TR-05 | Validate exclusive pathways and overlapping occupations. | TSA HME and FMCSA HOS, SRC-0054/0074 | Partition shares sum to one; nested SOC groups are flagged. |
| TR-06 | Preserve alternative compensation methods and denominators. | TSA flight training, OSHA extinguishers, BLS NCS | Direct compensation and wage/compensation-share remain distinct. |
| TR-07 | Model overhead components, allocation bases and overlap. | EPA PCB and EBSA, SRC-0056/0102 | Industry-to-occupation matrices reproduce; profit is not silently treated as internal labor cost. |
| TR-08 | Maintain an obligation ledger across controls. | BLS SOII, FDA preventive controls, CMS hospital | Transfers and exclusions identify controls, baselines and effects. |
| TR-09 | Separate internal hours from outside services and preserve agency conventions. | OSHA extinguishers and EBSA claims | Outsourced activity is charged once; classification deviations are documented. |
| TR-10 | Separate gross resource cost, fees, offsets and broader benefits. | CBP pipeline, USCIS I-751, TSA fee programs | Unknown costs cannot be replaced by claimed savings. |
| TR-11 | Model capital stock, purchase/replacement cohorts, life and horizon. | EPA CGP and FMCSA ELDs | Annual purchases are not divided by approval years without justification. |
| TR-12 | Federal costs expose workload and contract/system allocations. | TSA aircraft operator, FCC satellite, PHMSA approvals | Staff counts multiply hours and narrative rates match tables. |
| TR-13 | Generate separate bridges for responses, hours and Item 13 dollars. | FCC IPCS, SRC-0064 | 6690 + 5900 + 1760 + 825 = 15175, with reasons and classifications. |
| TR-14 | Maintain multiple named baselines. | FCC notice revision and FERC amendment | Notice, approval and analytical baselines are never silently substituted. |
| TR-15 | Support statistical model nodes alongside workload equations. | IRS business tax, SRC-0094 | Coefficients, calibration, restricted inputs and replication evidence are inventoried. |
| TR-16 | Store validation observations with measurement scope. | Census AIES, SRC-0099 printed page 19 | Sample, segment and statistic accompany observations; means and medians remain distinct. |
| TR-17 | Separate model recalibration from requirement changes. | IRS Item 15 | Time-to-purchased-service redistribution appears in the change ledger. |
| TR-18 | Identify stale sources and unsupported assumptions. | EPA TRI constants and TSA HME growth | Refresh reports distinguish old evidence from unsupported extrapolation. |
| TR-19 | Check workbook formulas independently of caches. | EPA CGP, SRC-0023 | Formula, cached value and independent result are retained. |
| TR-20 | Distinguish zero, missing and not applicable. | SEC interactive data versus BLS SOII | Deferred federal cost remains missing; a justified zero can earn full credit. |

Narrative generation must mark unresolved material inputs for analyst judgment. Defaults should preserve evidence without encouraging unsupported precision.

Freeze note: specification0.5.0 is frozen with M1-1.0.0. Later evidence supplies acceptance examples for existing requirements: TSA TWIC pathway and fee ledgers(TR-05/10), Coast Guard removed-addendum bridge(TR-08/13), CMMC internal/vendor/system separation(TR-07/10/12), EPA CEMS explicit annuity(TR-11), FinCEN nonfiling case funnels(TR-04/08), and NASS advance/nonresponse activities(TR-04/16). No new major requirement was needed after model0.5.0.
tsa-comparison:
# TSA gap analysis

Ten TSA collections score 50–76, mean 67.4, under rubric1.0.0. The best supported characterization is **inconsistent public reconstruction quality, with several strong methods**. This purposive sample cannot establish that TSA is typical or unusually rigorous across the federal population. It does not support unique or universal best-in-class practice. Other collections equal or exceed TSA in meaningful dimensions, including close security and workplace-compliance comparators.

TSA flight training scores52/60 on the Item12 composite, close to BLS SOII/NCS at53. TSA aircraft operators, airports and TWIC provide useful activity and pathway models. Gaps recur in assumption support, occupation-to-task matching, fees versus resources, precision and Item15 driver bridges.

| Action | Method or gap | Evidence and implication |
|---|---|---|
| KEEP | Explicit SOC/NAICS, wage selection and benefits ratios | Flight training SRC-0036 Item12 footnotes: preserve entry-career rationale and source vintages. |
| KEEP | Atomic activities and employer/applicant effort | Aircraft operators SRC-0038; airports SRC-0176 Item12: retain equations and federal salary denominators. |
| KEEP | Transition cohorts and exclusive enrollment pathways | Flight training SRC-0036; TWIC SRC-0180 Tables1–9: retain years and paths before averaging. |
| IMPROVE | Population partitions, rate periods and units | HME SRC-0054; surface cyber SRC-0022: online subsets must not be added to full in-person burden; monthly turnover is not an annual contact-change probability. |
| IMPROVE | Occupational weights matched to tasks | TWIC SRC-0180 wage table: national truck drivers dominate its basket; employment shares need validation as task weights. |
| IMPROVE | Footnotes, rates, fees and narrative totals | Airports SRC-0176; certified cargo SRC-0040; Secure Flight SRC-0048: generate all outputs from one model. |
| IMPROVE | Federal resources distinct from fee revenue | TWIC SRC-0180 Item14 and flight training SRC-0036: fee recovery does not reconstruct staff, contracts or systems. |
| ADOPT | Exact driver bridges and named baselines | FCC IPCS SRC-0064 Item15; OSHA process safety SRC-0187 Table3: link approval, notice, input changes and classifications. |
| ADOPT | Burden measurement with task scope and distributions | Census AIES SRC-0099 printed page19: preparation, questionnaire estimates and paradata differ. |
| ADOPT | Cross-control obligation and make-or-buy ledgers | BLS SOII SRC-0008; OSHA extinguishers SRC-0060: avoid double counting requirements and purchased work. |
| ADOPT | Coverage adjustments, case funnels and nonfiling work | OSHA process safety SRC-0187 Item12; FinCEN SRC-0191 pp31605–31611: preserve proxy assumptions and excluded stages. |
| ADOPT | Distinct asset life, replacement cohorts and approval horizon | EPA CEMS SRC-0161/0162; chemical reporting SRC-0183 Tables3–4: use current inputs and explicit PRA mapping. |
| INVESTIGATE | Occupational overhead allocation | EBSA SRC-0102 Tables1–3: replicate and correct its worked example; retain valid alternatives. |
| INVESTIGATE | Workload system allocation and vendor/internal prices | CMMC SRC-0164; ETA SRC-0144 Item14: separate allocation drivers and vendor profit. |
| INVESTIGATE | Statistical calibration where complexity warrants | IRS SRC-0094: accessible coefficients or controlled replication protocol needed. |
| INVESTIGATE | Effect of TSA's reported overhaul | Surface cyber submitted2026-09-01; HME2026-08-21, both pending at retrieval. Dates do not establish process adoption. |

The hypothesis's uniqueness/best-practice implication is not supported. Its causal motivation claim remains unestablished: public statements cannot tell why TSA invests in analysis. EBSA explicitly shares methods across PRA and regulatory-impact analysis (SRC-0102); CMMC directly connects ICR burden with regulatory analysis (SRC-0164). Downstream analytical reuse is not unique to TSA. See calibration.md and research/limitations.md for inference boundaries.
